title: Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · abstract-1-1】Gallbladder carcinoma (GBC) is the most common biliary tract malignancy and is usually diagnosed at an advanced stage. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), is increasingly applied to its diagnosis, surgical management and prognostication, but how far the reported performance can be trusted is unclear.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar were searched to 5 May 2026 using database-specific search strategies. Each primary prediction-model study was characterized separately by design, number of centers and validation type (internal, temporal or external).

【Results · abstract-3-1】Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. The best recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.76 on internal (random-split) validation; none of the reviewed prognostic models reported a quantified external-validation estimate. Intraoperative AI is technically feasible but has no outcome data, and federated learning has been tested only in simulation.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Artificial Intelligence in Gallbladder Carcinoma: A Review of Research Studies and Clinical Evidence》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Of 31 primary AI studies in GBC, 29 were retrospective, 22 were single-center and 24 reported internal validation only. In independent test or external cohorts, DL and ML models discriminated benign from malignant gallbladder lesions with areas under the curve (AUCs) of approximately 0.80-0.89; a multicenter model distinguishing xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis from GBC achieved an external AUC of 0.88, and automated computed tomography (CT) segmentation an external Dice score of 0.76. The best recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.76 on internal (random-split) validation; none of the reviewed prognostic models reported a quantified external-validation estimate. Intraoperative AI is technically feasible but has no outcome data, and federated learning has been tested only in simulation.

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】AI could plausibly assist several steps of GBC care, but the evidence is dominated by retrospective, single-center, internally validated studies from Asia, and metrics from different studies are not directly comparable. Prospective multicenter external validation, shared annotated datasets and standardized reporting are required before clinical adoption.
